name: Thalvex
manufacturer: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals (licensed); Nightshade Pharmatech (gray market variant)
description: Thalvex is a targeted SNT-interface anxiolytic that works specifically during the sleep-onset transition, preventing the hypervigilant neural state that causes pre-sleep anxiety spirals, intrusive memories, and the immediate-REM nightmares common in severe PTSD and chrome-rejection syndrome. Unlike Sombrevex, which operates throughout sleep, Thalvex acts only in the first 45 minutes, allowing natural dream processing to proceed once the fear-onset window closes.
effects: Prevents intrusive memory cascade during hypnagogic state
Allows natural dream content once fear-onset window passes
Preserved emotional processing during sleep — less blunting than full-spectrum suppressors
side_effects: Hypnagogic hallucinations in 15% of users — vivid but non-frightening visuals during onset
Vapor delivery inconsistent in polluted Shelf air — dosing unreliable
Nightshade's gray market variant contains an undisclosed stimulant to extend shelf life that causes heart palpitations
Psychological dependency on the onset experience — users feel unable to begin sleep without it
duration: 45-minute active window at sleep onset; effects persist through natural sleep cycle
street_price: Φ28 per inhaler (Lazarus, 10 doses); Φ14 per inhaler (Nightshade, 10 doses)
cultural_context: Thalvex is the drug that chrome-rejection survivors call 'the difference between trying to sleep and being able to.' Chrome-rejection syndrome — where the immune system attacks cyberware integration points — causes a specific variety of violent hypnagogic nightmare that Sombrevex is too blunt to address without emotional zombification. Thalvex found its market by being precise. The Nightshade variant, cheaper and more accessible, has spread aggressively on the Shelf despite its documented cardiac risks — Nightshade's legal team argues the risks are within acceptable parameters for Tier 1.
story_hooks: A chrome-rejection support group on the Shelf has been using the Nightshade Thalvex variant for six months — now three members have died of cardiac events, and the group wants someone to prove Nightshade knew about the risk before they shipped the batch.

The hypnagogic hallucinations that Thalvex produces in 15% of users have been reported with a disturbing consistency: multiple unconnected users across different tiers are seeing the same figure during their onset visions — a woman in a white coat who appears to be trying to say something.

A Lazarus Pharmaceuticals rep approaches a fixer with a contract: find out how Nightshade is undercutting their Thalvex price by half without apparently losing margin — and whether the answer involves something in the formula that Lazarus hasn't yet detected.
